segments.title: Johannesburg's strong week, a sharp day in Harare
segments.say: Johannesburg had a strong week. Harare had a sharp fall on Thursday. And the V F E X had big moves in two familiar names. This is Reian Creative Finance. Understanding markets. Following capital.

segments.name: JSE All Share
facts: Up about 3.96% over the week (from 104,638.77 on 20 Nov)
Rand around R17.42 per US$ on Friday morning
segments.note: Sources: Yahoo Finance daily data; DailyInvestor (27 Nov 2026). Week change is our calculation.
segments.say: Let's start in Johannesburg. The J S E All Share Index closed on Friday at 108,783, up 2.02 percent on the day. Over the whole week it gained about 4 percent, from 104,639 the Friday before. The rand was trading around 17 rand 42 to the US dollar on Friday morning.

segments.title: Metals and global risk appetite
points: Gold, platinum and copper rose sharply on Friday (see Video 1)
JSE is heavy in miners, so metal prices matter
A week earlier the JSE had fallen over 3.6% in one day on dollar strength
Reports say the Top 40 index passed 100,000 points
segments.note: Sources: Moneyweb (prior week); Daily News Egypt Africa (27 Nov); Yahoo Finance. Linking metals to the JSE move is our interpretation.
segments.say: Why? Johannesburg is packed with mining companies, and gold, platinum and copper all rose sharply on Friday. That's our reading of it, not an official explanation. It's quite a swing: Moneyweb reported that a week earlier the J S E fell more than 3.6 percent in a single day on dollar strength. Reports this week also say the Top 40 index passed 100,000 points.

segments.name: ZSE All Share
facts: Friday 27 Nov data not yet published when we checked
segments.note: Sources: zse.co.zw market activity; AfricanFinancials (26 Nov 2026). Previous close derived from the published points change.
segments.say: Now Harare. The latest Z S E data we could verify is from Thursday, the twenty sixth. The All Share Index fell 3.22 percent to 496.40, and the Top 10 index lost 3.9 percent. Friday's figures had not been published when we checked, so we're not guessing them.

segments.title: Biggest movers on Thursday
segments.note: Source: AfricanFinancials, 26 Nov 2026. ZimRe also +4.69%. Daily moves only; prices in ZWG.
segments.say: The biggest movers on Thursday. Gainers: Turnall up 7.1 percent, C B Z up 6.5, and Willdale up 4.7. Losers: Hippo Valley, British American Tobacco and N M B Z each fell more than 14 percent. Moves that big on one day are a reminder that Z S E shares can be thinly traded.

segments.title: Victoria Falls: Friday's movers
segments.note: Source: AfricanFinancials, 27 Nov 2026 (prices in US cents). The VFEX All Share index value for the day could not be verified.
segments.say: On the V F E X, where everything trades in US dollars, Caledonia Mining jumped 17.4 percent on Friday, a gold miner on a strong gold day. Invictus rose 7.8 percent. Simbisa fell 8.4 percent and Seed Co 5.9 percent. We could not verify a dated V F E X All Share Index value for Friday, so we're not quoting one.

segments.title: An IPO on the calendar
points: Amalgamated Brands: reported US$20m IPO on the VFEX at US$0.35 a share
Of that, about US$5m is reported to be new shares
Trading is reported to be planned for 7 December 2026
We'll explain IPOs step by step in our listing series
segments.note: Source: news reports (see source register). Not yet listed; details may change. Not a recommendation to buy.
segments.say: One to watch. News reports say Amalgamated Brands is raising about 20 million US dollars in an I P O on the V F E X, at 35 US cents a share, with about 5 million of that in new shares, and trading planned for the seventh of December. It hasn't listed yet, so details may change. We explain exactly how I P Os work in our listing series.

segments.title: Who can own Zimbabwean shares?
points: Under RBZ guidelines, foreigners can hold up to 49% of a ZSE- or FINSEC-listed company
No single foreign investor can hold more than 15%
Zimbabweans in the diaspora are not limited
Listing abroad needs prior RBZ approval
segments.note: Source: RBZ Foreign Exchange Transactions Guidelines (March 2026), ss.4.2.8 and 4.2.18. Educational summary; check the current text.
segments.say: A useful rule to know. Under the Reserve Bank's March 2026 foreign exchange guidelines, non resident investors can together own up to 49 percent of a company on the Z S E or FINSEC, with no single foreign investor above 15 percent. Zimbabweans in the diaspora are not limited. And a local company that wants to list on a foreign exchange needs prior Reserve Bank approval.

segments.title: What to take from this week
points: Johannesburg follows global metals and the dollar
Harare can move sharply on low volumes
The VFEX gives US-dollar exposure, with fewer, larger moves per stock
Always check the date on any price you read
segments.note: Interpretation by Reian Creative Finance. Not investment advice.
segments.say: So, the African picture. Johannesburg follows global metal prices and the dollar. Harare can move sharply on small volumes. The V F E X gives US dollar exposure, but individual shares can jump or drop a lot in a day. And always check the date on any price you read.
